source: Demirer, Fradkin, Tadelis, Peng (2025), NBER WP 34608
title: The Emerging Market for Intelligence: Pricing, Supply, and Demand for LLMs

six_facts.claim: Rapid growth in number of models, creators, and inference providers; open-source entrants drive the growth.
Price declines + persistent price heterogeneity across and within intelligence tiers. Open-source ~90% cheaper than closed-source at same intelligence tier.
six_facts.essay_relevance: Load-bearing for resilience sketch; complicates production-centric sovereignty framing.

six_facts.claim: Market dynamism — frequent turnover among leading models and creators.
Horizontal and vertical differentiation — no single model dominates across use cases.
six_facts.essay_relevance: Complicates simple top-3-provider chokepoint framing. Concentration at API layer ≠ concentration at task/use-case layer.

six_facts.claim: Short-run price elasticities just above 1 — limited scope for Jevons-paradox effects.
Multi-homing increasing over time but most firms still concentrate on a single model.
six_facts.essay_relevance: Consistent with Menlo Ventures 11% vendor switching figure when framed carefully.
